comments.text:
I lived in Newfoundland from 1973 to 1979, starting in high school as a Landed Immigrant (equivalent to “resident alien” here in the States). 

I was surprised to learn in the video that the government added “Labrador” to “Newfoundland” upon Confederation with Canada. I never heard that while I was there, though it could be. Perhaps it just wasn't emphasized.

We always used the postal abbreviation “NF” while we lived there and never saw “NL” until well after I came back to the States in 1980.

Some trivia the video never mentioned was that, whereas Canada and Australia (and probably New Zealand) had the capitalized word “Dominion” in their name, as in the “Dominion of Canada”. Newfoundland was also a dominion, of course, but it went by the name “Newfoundland” without the word “Dominion.”

My mother was born a British subject in Newfoundland in 1928. Since she never became a U.S. citizen, her citizenship became Canadian when Newfoundland became a province of Canada in 1949.

Consequently, Parliament conferred Canadian citizenship on my siblings and me when the law changed back in the 1980s.
